text:
Sidney Crosby passed Marcel Dionne last night in Los Angeles and now stands alone in sixth on the NHL's all-time scoring list with 1,772 points, 26 behind Ron Francis, as Ryan Wilson of Hockey Hot Stove noted. It was the bright spot in a bleak stretch. The Penguins won 5-2 to end a four-game winless run, but Wilson also pointed out they are tied for the fewest points in the Eastern Conference, and the conversation around the team has turned toward the exits: Evgeni Malkin has to submit a three-team trade list, the Penguins are reportedly fielding calls on Rickard Rakell, and several outlets are asking how much longer Crosby plays. Our numbers give Pittsburgh a 20% shot at the playoffs.

The strange part is that Pittsburgh's process is fine. The Penguins have taken 52% of the five-on-five expected goals (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and their 14 points trail the 17.8 their chances deserve. Arturs Silovs (.876) has not helped. They play the second night of a back-to-back without Bryan Rust, whose spot beside Crosby and Rakell has gone to Tommy Novak, who scored twice in the first 5:10 last night.

Anaheim is having the opposite season. The Ducks have won four straight, and they have done it by finishing: 21 goals on 12.8 expected in those games, 45% of the five-on-five expected goals on the year. Cutter Gauthier is the headline, with goals in five straight games (ten in all) inside a seven-game point streak, and NHL.com has him making history with his goal and power-play streaks. Leo Carlsson has 15 points in his own seven-game run. Beckett Sennecke plays his 100th game.

Our sleepers are Judd Caulfield, whose 4.4 expected goals in his last ten games lead every depth forward in our numbers, and Pittsburgh's Ben Kindel, 45% for a point against a 38% season pace. Laurent Brossoit (.847) starts for Anaheim, so the Penguins' shooters have a chance to change the mood. Our numbers make it 3.42 expected goals to 3.22 for the Ducks.
headline: Crosby climbs, the Penguins sink, and the Ducks can't miss

hunch.text: The Ducks have scored 21 goals on 12.8 expected during their streak, and that kind of finishing doesn't last. Our gut says the Penguins, who have had the better of five-on-five play all season, catch Anaheim on the night it cools off.
